name: windows
title: Windows
description: Every open window, with its app's icon, most recently used first and grouped by app. Enter switches to it; close, minimise, close or minimise all of the app, and hide or show the app from the action panel. Spaces: a row per Space, workspace or desktop with the apps on it; Enter brings it in front, and named desktops take global hotkeys.
author: pal

settings.label: Minimised windows
settings.description: Focusing a minimised window restores it.

settings.label: Space names
settings.description: Names for the desktops by number: the first entry names Desktop 1. A named space's row is titled by it, the windows rows say `ws <name>`, and its row id is the name, so `[palettes.windows-spaces.item_hotkeys]` reads `term = "ctrl+alt+shift+a"`.

settings.label: Back and forth
settings.text: A space's hotkey pressed while on it goes to the previous space
settings.description: Hyprland's workspace_back_and_forth: the same key toggles between a space and where you came from. Enter on the current space's row does the same.

settings.label: Toggle pair
settings.description: Two space names (or numbers) the Toggle row flips between: on the first it goes to the second, anywhere else to the first. toggle = "ctrl+f" under item_hotkeys makes it a key.

store.tagline: Every open window, most recently used first, and the spaces they are on; Enter switches
features: Live: listed again every time the panel shows, so window titles are root results and the order is most recently used, the window you came from first (macOS and Hyprland)
A section per app; the app name is the subtitle and a keyword, the bundle id or window class a keyword too

Spaces: a row per Space, workspace or desktop in the desktop's order, the apps on it as the subtitle, the icon of the window used there last, `current` and `previous` tags; Enter brings it in front (macOS: an instant switch by the same synthesised swipe yabai uses, then the window used there last raised), Previous space goes back, Toggle flips between two named spaces, and a named desktop's row takes an `item_hotkeys` key
A hidden app's window carries a `hidden` tag, a minimised one `minimized`, one on another space `other space` or `ws 3`, and the monitor when known
Close (`cmd+w`) and Minimize (`cmd+m`) keep the palette open and list again; Hide app (`cmd+h`) hides the whole app, Show app (`cmd+shift+h`) brings a hidden one back
Minimize all (`cmd+shift+m`) and Close all (`cmd+shift+w`, asks first) act on every window of the app
Hyprland, Sway and X11 (wmctrl) on Linux, detected rather than configured

actions.title: Focus
actions.description: Hides the panel, then raises the window, restoring it if minimised.

actions.title: Close
actions.description: The palette stays open and lists again.

actions.title: Minimize
actions.description: Not offered on a window that already is.

actions.title: Hide app
actions.description: macOS: hides the window's process through System Events. Not offered on a hidden app.

actions.title: Show app
actions.description: macOS, on a hidden app's window: the app comes forward with every window it had; the panel hides.

actions.title: Minimize all of this app
actions.description: On an app with more than one window.

actions.title: Go
actions.description: Spaces: hides the panel, then brings the space in front. On the current space with Back and forth on, goes to the previous one.

windows.description: What is open right now, most recently used first.

keys.title: Minimize all of the app's windows
Close all of the app's windows, after a confirm

spaces.title: Spaces
spaces.description: Every Space, workspace or desktop in the desktop's order, with the apps on it; Enter brings it in front. Previous space goes back to the one left most recently; Toggle flips between the two spaces named in the setting.
